instruction.name: xvldrepl.w
instruction.description: Read 32-bit data from memory address `addr + offset`, replicate the data to all vector lanes and save into `dst`. Address misalignment does not raise an exception. The `offset` operand is a byte offset, matching the assembly immediate; the encoded instruction stores it as a scaled immediate for wider elements.

experiments.name: pick-based address chase
experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 8000 --unroll2 16000 --iters 50 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; st.d $r20, $r20, 0; addi.d $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r21, 0; li.d $r5, 1' --asm 'xvldrepl.w $xr0, $r20, 0; xvpickve2gr.w $r4, $xr0, 0; add.d $r20, $r20, $r4'

latencies.notes: L1D hit. 11 measured cycles less the 5-cycle pick and 1 cycle of add.d give 5, the same as the LSX form.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: xvldrepl.w $xr0, $r20, 0; xvldrepl.w $xr1, $r20, 4; xvldrepl.w $xr2, $r20, 8; xvldrepl.w $xr3, $r20, 12; xvldrepl.w $xr4, $r20, 16; xvldrepl.w $xr5, $r20, 20; xvldrepl.w $xr6, $r20, 24; xvldrepl.w $xr7, $r20, 28
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r4, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r4' --asm 'xvldrepl.w $xr0, $r20, 0; xvldrepl.w $xr1, $r20, 4; xvldrepl.w $xr2, $r20, 8; xvldrepl.w $xr3, $r20, 12; xvldrepl.w $xr4, $r20, 16; xvldrepl.w $xr5, $r20, 20; xvldrepl.w $xr6, $r20, 24; xvldrepl.w $xr7, $r20, 28'
throughput.notes: 8 independent memory operations take 4.00 cycles. Buffer is 64-byte aligned; unaligned LASX loads/stores are substantially slower.

notes: L1D-hit replicating vector load; latency 4 cycles.
